textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 science · Reproduction: How Life Continues · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind.
beats.speakEn: Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind.

beats.en: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and gives offspring identical to it. Examples are binary fission, budding, fragmentation and vegetative propagation.
beats.speakEn: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and gives offspring identical to it. Examples are binary fission, budding, fragmentation and vegetative propagation.

type: Key Concept: Reproduction is the process by which organisms produce new individuals of their own kind.
Rule: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and gives offspring identical to it.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 9 science · Reproduction: How Life Continues · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of gametes, so offspring show variation.

beats.en: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of gametes, so offspring show variation.
beats.speakEn: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of gametes, so offspring show variation.

beats.en: In flowers, pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. It can be self or cross pollination, by wind, water, insects or animals.
beats.speakEn: In flowers, pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma. It can be self or cross pollination, by wind, water, insects or animals.

type: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of gametes, so offspring show variation.
